outline: 643 Area of Composite Figures with Special Quadrilaterals

examples.question_text: A composite figure consists of a rectangle with a trapezium on top. The rectangle is $12\text{ cm}$ wide. The trapezium's parallel sides are $12\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$, and its perpendicular height is $4\text{ cm}$. The whole figure is $10\text{ cm}$ high. Find its area.
examples.solution_text:
The rectangle's height is $10-4=6\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} A_1&=12\times6\\&=72\text{ cm}^2\\ A_2&=\frac{4}{2}(12+8)\\&=40\text{ cm}^2\\ A_{\text{Total}}&=72+40\\&=112\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A triangle sits on the shorter parallel side of a trapezium. The trapezium has parallel sides of $16\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $4\text{ cm}$. The whole figure is $13\text{ cm}$ high, measured perpendicular to its base. Find its area.
examples.solution_text:
The triangle's perpendicular height is $13-4=9\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} A_1&=\frac{4}{2}(16+10)\\&=52\text{ cm}^2\\ A_2&=\frac{10\times9}{2}\\&=45\text{ cm}^2\\ A_{\text{Total}}&=52+45\\&=97\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

Split horizontally through the tips.
$\begin{aligned} A_1&=\frac{4}{2}(6+10)\\&=32\text{ cm}^2\\ A_2&=\frac{4}{2}(10+6)\\&=32\text{ cm}^2\\ A_{\text{Total}}&=32+32\\&=64\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$
For a different split, draw vertical lines joining the top and bottom endpoints. The rectangle is $6\text{ cm}$ wide and $8\text{ cm}$ high. The two triangles' perpendicular heights add to $10-6=4\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} A_{\text{rectangle}}&=6\times8\\&=48\text{ cm}^2\\ A_{\text{triangles}}&=\frac{8\times4}{2}\\&=16\text{ cm}^2\\ A_{\text{Total}}&=48+16\\&=64\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A logo consists of a parallelogram joined along its full base to the shorter parallel side of a trapezium. The parallelogram has base $24\text{ mm}$ and perpendicular height $12\text{ mm}$. The trapezium has the same perpendicular height, and its longer parallel side is twice its shorter parallel side. Find the logo's area.
examples.solution_text:
The trapezium's parallel sides are $24\text{ mm}$ and $48\text{ mm}$.
$\begin{aligned} A_1&=24\times12\\&=288\text{ mm}^2\\ A_2&=\frac{12}{2}(24+48)\\&=432\text{ mm}^2\\ A_{\text{Total}}&=288+432\\&=720\text{ mm}^2\end{aligned}$
For a parallelogram, use the distance perpendicular to the chosen base, even when the base is vertical.

examples.question_text: A trapezium-shaped notch is removed from a rectangular sheet. The sheet is $10\text{ m}$ wide and $7\text{ m}$ high. The notch has parallel sides of $10\text{ m}$ and $4\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $2\text{ m}$; its longer side runs along the sheet's full top edge. Find the remaining area.
examples.solution_text: $\begin{aligned} A_1&=10\times7\\&=70\text{ m}^2\\ A_2&=\frac{2}{2}(10+4)\\&=14\text{ m}^2\\ A_{\text{remaining}}&=70-14\\&=56\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A trapezium-shaped hole lies entirely inside a trapezium-shaped panel. The panel's parallel sides are $22\text{ m}$ and $14\text{ m}$, with perpendicular height $10\text{ m}$. The hole's parallel sides are $10\text{ m}$ and $6\text{ m}$, with perpendicular height $3\text{ m}$. Find the remaining area.

A barn wall is a rectangle with a triangle on top. It is $6\text{ m}$ wide, both vertical sides are $3\text{ m}$ high, and its highest point is $4.5\text{ m}$ above the horizontal ground. Find the area to paint.
examples.solution_text:
The triangle's perpendicular height is $4.5-3=1.5\text{ m}$.
$\begin{aligned} A_1&=6\times3\\&=18\text{ m}^2\\ A_2&=\frac{6\times1.5}{2}\\&=4.5\text{ m}^2\\ A_{\text{Total}}&=18+4.5\\&=22.5\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A cross-section consists of a rectangle on the left and a trapezium on the right. The rectangle is $2\text{ m}$ wide and $8\text{ m}$ high. The total horizontal width is $5\text{ m}$. The trapezium's parallel sides are vertical: its left side is the rectangle's full right edge, and its right side is $4\text{ m}$ high. Find the cross-section's area.
examples.solution_text:
The distance perpendicular to the trapezium's vertical parallel sides is $5-2=3\text{ m}$.
$\begin{aligned} A_1&=2\times8\\&=16\text{ m}^2\\ A_2&=\frac{3}{2}(8+4)\\&=18\text{ m}^2\\ A_{\text{Total}}&=16+18\\&=34\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$

The dashed shared side separates the rhombus from the rectangle.
$\begin{aligned} A_1&=\frac{12\times16}{2}\\&=96\text{ cm}^2\\ A_2&=10\times3\\&=30\text{ cm}^2\\ A_{\text{Total}}&=96+30\\&=126\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A rhombus-shaped hole is cut from a kite-shaped card. The kite has diagonals $14\text{ cm}$ and $20\text{ cm}$. The hole lies entirely inside it and has diagonals $6\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$. Find the remaining area.
examples.solution_text: $\begin{aligned} A_1&=\frac{14\times20}{2}\\&=140\text{ cm}^2\\ A_2&=\frac{6\times10}{2}\\&=30\text{ cm}^2\\ A_{\text{remaining}}&=140-30\\&=110\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A sign consists of a central square with an isosceles triangle joined externally to each of its left and right sides. The square has side length $6\text{ m}$. The triangle tips lie on the horizontal line through the square's centre and are $20\text{ m}$ apart. Find the total area.
examples.solution_text:
The two triangles' perpendicular heights add to $20-6=14\text{ m}$; their individual heights are not needed.
$\begin{aligned} A_1&=6\times6\\&=36\text{ m}^2\\ A_2+A_3&=\frac{6\times14}{2}\\&=42\text{ m}^2\\ A_{\text{Total}}&=36+42\\&=78\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A square-shaped hole is cut from a kite-shaped card. Each square diagonal is $8\text{ cm}$. Its left and right vertices coincide with the kite's left and right vertices, and their vertical diagonals lie on the same line. The kite extends $3\text{ cm}$ above the square's top vertex and $5\text{ cm}$ below its bottom vertex. Find the remaining area.
examples.solution_text:
The kite's vertical diagonal is $3+8+5=16\text{ cm}$. Its horizontal diagonal is $8\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{aligned} A_1&=\frac{8\times16}{2}\\&=64\text{ cm}^2\\ A_2&=\frac{8\times8}{2}\\&=32\text{ cm}^2\\ A_{\text{remaining}}&=64-32\\&=32\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Rectangle height = 10−4 = 6 cm. Rectangle area = 12×6 = 72 cm²; trapezium area = 4(12+8)/2 = 40 cm². Total = 112 cm².
Triangle height = 13−4 = 9 cm. Trapezium area = 4(16+10)/2 = 52 cm²; triangle area = 10×9/2 = 45 cm². Total = 97 cm².

Each trapezium has area 4(6+10)/2 = 32 cm², giving 64 cm². Independently, the central rectangle has area 6×8 = 48 cm²; the end triangles together have area 8(10−6)/2 = 16 cm². Total = 64 cm². Diagram coordinates support both splits.
Shared base = 24 mm; longer trapezium base = 48 mm. Parallelogram area = 24×12 = 288 mm²; trapezium area = 12(24+48)/2 = 432 mm². Total = 720 mm².
Rectangle area = 10×7 = 70 m²; notch area = 2(10+4)/2 = 14 m². Remaining area = 56 m².
Panel area = 10(22+14)/2 = 180 m²; hole area = 3(10+6)/2 = 24 m². Remaining area = 156 m².
Roof triangle height = 4.5−3 = 1.5 m. Rectangle area = 6×3 = 18 m²; triangle area = 6×1.5/2 = 4.5 m². Total = 22.5 m².
Horizontal separation of the vertical parallel sides = 5−2 = 3 m. Rectangle area = 2×8 = 16 m²; trapezium area = 3(8+4)/2 = 18 m². Total = 34 m².

Rhombus area = 12×16/2 = 96 cm²; rectangle area = 10×3 = 30 cm². Total = 126 cm². Rhombus half-diagonals 6 and 8 give side length 10 cm. The rectangle offset (1.8,2.4) has length 3 and is perpendicular to shared-side vector (8,−6); the diagram and right-angle mark agree.
Kite area = 14×20/2 = 140 cm²; rhombus hole area = 6×10/2 = 30 cm². Remaining area = 110 cm². This adapts the source's subtraction of diagonal-based quadrilateral areas.
Combined triangle heights = 20−6 = 14 m. Square area = 36 m²; combined triangle area = 6×14/2 = 42 m². Total = 78 m²; individual triangle heights are unnecessary.
Kite diagonals are 8 cm and 3+8+5 = 16 cm. Kite area = 8×16/2 = 64 cm²; square area = 8×8/2 = 32 cm². Remaining area = 32 cm².
